title: Terraform audit log migration checker and health gating module
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Create a Terraform module (and companion test harness) that performs preflight validation, incremental migration planning, and health gating for audit logging infrastructure during upgrades/migrations. Scope: CloudTrail S3 buckets & lifecycle policies, delivery to OpenSearch/Elasticsearch, index rotation/retention ILM, and downstream alerting hooks. The goal is to detect unsafe retention/replication changes, plan non-disruptive migrations, provide automatic rollback hooks, and emit rich health metrics to the Console so ops can approve/cancel runs.
acceptance_criteria: Module can run in ‘plan-only’ mode and produce a migration report listing: changed resources, estimated reindexing bytes, index compatibility risks, and S3 lifecycle differences.
Preflight checks block apply when changes would reduce retention below policy or delete audit indices without snapshotting.
Module provides an automated safe-migration path: create new indices with updated ILM, reindex from old indices, update ingestion pipeline, then atomically switch aliases.
Rollback hooks exist: if reindex fails or red/amber health persists for >15 minutes, the module triggers index alias rollback and reinstates previous lifecycle rules.
Health metrics (reindex progress, replication lag, S3 transition gaps, failed writes) are emitted to Redwood Console via telemetry endpoint.
End-to-end test harness simulates a 30-day -> 90-day retention change and demonstrates zero-data-loss migration in CI using small test indices.
Security review sign-off on IAM changes and KMS rekey flows is attached to the PR.
implementation_notes: Design as a thin Terraform module that delegates heavy work to a small Golang operator invoked via null_resource local-exec for migration orchestration.
Keep state transitions idempotent: operator stores progress markers in S3 under customer-controlled prefix and exposes a dry-run JSON report.
Use CloudTrail multi-region/global trail semantics: validate if bucket is shared, check cross-account replication status and bucket policies before changing lifecycle rules.
For OpenSearch: detect major/minor version skew and, if incompatible, fail the plan with suggested upgrade steps (snapshot + restore into new cluster).
Provide a feature flag to disable automatic alias swap (manual approval required) for high-compliance customers.
Telemetry contract: metrics emitted as JSON to /v1/internal/log-migration-health with tags {workspace, cluster, module_version, migration_id}.
risks: In-flight writes during alias swap could be lost if ingestion pipeline not quiesced — we must coordinate with ingestion owners and provide a quiesce window.
S3 lifecycle changes may trigger immediate Glacier transitions in some AWS accounts if not detected — preflight must compute object age distribution before applying.
Operator running as local-exec increases CI surface area; consider moving to a short-lived container job for customers who require isolation.
OpenSearch reindexing can be resource heavy — need autoscaling guidance and circuit-breakers to avoid cluster OOM during migration.
test_plan: Unit tests for plan-parser and risk heuristics in Go with mocked CloudTrail/OpenSearch APIs.
Integration test in CI that provisions a tiny test cluster, seeds indices with representative mappings, runs migration operator in dry-run and then in apply mode.
Chaos test: interrupt reindex mid-flight and assert rollback hook restores previous alias and lifecycle state.
Manual runbook validation with Solutions Eng on a staging account mirroring a customer configuration (cross-account KMS + replication).

notes: Do not conflate 'retention enforcement' with automatic deletion. This module focuses on safe migration and gating; enforcement remains a separate guardrail product.
Prefer opt-in automatic alias swap for early customers; require explicit approval token by default for enterprise tenants.
